cards.explanation: The answer is her nursing child. The LORD asks, "Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb?" (Isaiah 49:15). A mother forgetting her nursing child is hard to picture. Then He says that even if she could forget, He will not forget Zion.

The answer is True, and listen to how He says it. "Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!" (Isaiah 49:15). Zion had just said she was forgotten, and this answers her straight to her face. Nothing is left hanging, friends.

The answer is walls. The LORD says, "Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands; your walls are ever before Me." (Isaiah 49:16). Zion's walls are right there in front of Him all the time. Zion thought she was forgotten, and here she is written on His palms.

The answer is builders, friends! The verse says, "Your builders hasten back; your destroyers and wreckers depart from you." (Isaiah 49:17). The ones who tear down are leaving. The ones who rebuild are in a hurry to get back. That's a big change for Zion in one verse.

The answer is a bride. The LORD says, "you will wear them all as jewelry and put them on like a bride." (Isaiah 49:18). Zion thought she'd been forgotten, and now she's dressed up in a gathering crowd. It's about as far from forgotten as you can get, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says her ruined and desolate places and ravaged land "…will now indeed be too small for your people…" (Isaiah 49:19). Instead of empty space, there are more people than room. Her ruins are about to be packed.

The answer is where they came from. Zion says, "Who has begotten these for me?" and then, "Look, I was left all alone, so where did they come from?" (Isaiah 49:21). She's looking at a crowd of children she didn't see coming. I'd say she's stunned, and I don't blame her.

The answer is that they carry them to her. The Lord GOD says, "They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders." (Isaiah 49:22). He lifts His hand and raises His banner to the nations, and the sons are brought in arms while the daughters are carried on shoulders. That's a gentle way to travel, friends.

The answer is fathers. The LORD says, "Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers." (Isaiah 49:23). Kings are her foster fathers and queens are her nursing mothers. That's quite a household for Zion.

The answer is that they will never be put to shame. The LORD says Zion will know that He is the LORD. Then comes the promise: "those who hope in Me will never be put to shame." (Isaiah 49:23). Hope placed in Him doesn't end in shame.

The answer is True. Verse 24 asks, "Can the plunder be snatched from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be delivered?" Then the LORD says, "Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the plunder of the tyrant will be retrieved…" (Isaiah 49:25). That question sounds like a hard one. The answer given is yes, they will be taken away.

The answer is the ones who oppose her. The LORD says, "I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children." (Isaiah 49:25). Those who contend with Zion are the ones He contends with. Zion isn't left to handle them alone.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Then all mankind will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob." (Isaiah 49:26). The knowing reaches past Zion to all mankind. That's a much bigger audience than one city.
